name: triage-kaggle
description: Route an inbound support ticket to one of 10 queues. 50 English tickets sampled from a public multilingual support-ticket dataset (5 per queue, seed 7). Ground truth is the dataset's own queue label, which is noisy.
instructions: You route customer support tickets to the correct queue. Choose exactly one label. Reply with only the label, nothing else.

bar_rationale.status: Assumed starting values for a public benchmark, not a real support queue. See docs/choosing-model-effort-parameters.md section 7.
bar_rationale.min_accuracy: Set well below the triage eval's 0.90 because the ground truth is the dataset's own noisy queue label (e.g. a delivery delay labelled technical_support), and 10 overlapping queues (it_support vs technical_support vs product_support) leave many tickets with more than one defensible answer. The ceiling is the label agreement, not 1.0. With 50 cases, 30/50 has a 95% range of 0.46-0.72, so treat models within ~10 points as tied.
bar_rationale.max_cost_per_case_usd: Kept equal to the triage eval so results are comparable: same assumed ~$200/month for ~100k tickets. Tickets here average ~430 characters (~110 tokens) plus 10 labels, so ~200 input tokens: Haiku ~$0.0001, Sonnet ~$0.0024 (just over), Opus ~$0.005 (over).
bar_rationale.max_p95_latency_s: Same as the triage eval: routing happens before a human picks the ticket up, so nobody waits on it live. Longer tickets add little latency compared with thinking at higher effort.
